title: FBI Investigating Apparent Hack of Key National Crime Database
summary:
The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of one of its most important databases, a person familiar with the matter said on Saturday. The database is called the National Crime Information Center, or NCIC. It is a giant computerized file that police officers across the country rely on every day. It holds records on fugitives, missing persons, criminal histories, stolen property, and more, and it is shared with local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies.

The FBI declined to comment on Saturday about the apparent hack, which was first reported by CNN and confirmed to The Associated Press by a person familiar with the matter. The person was not authorized to speak publicly, so they spoke on the condition of anonymity. The scope of the problem was not immediately clear. Investigators have not said what, if anything, was taken or changed.

Asked about it on Saturday, President Donald Trump said in a Fox News interview, "We just heard about it and I will say that it's not good." The news comes after a run of digital outages in government and private systems. Trump administration officials have said those outages were caused by routine efforts to upgrade computer systems and fix weak spots, rather than by a cyberattack. There was no immediate sign that the FBI incident was connected to those outages.

The FBI has been a frequent target for hackers before. In September, the bureau said it was investigating a hack of its job portal website after a hacking group known as ShinyHunters claimed it had obtained a large trove of data on bureau employees and applicants. In March, the FBI said it was investigating "suspicious activities" on an internal system holding sensitive information about surveillance operations and investigations.
why_it_matters: Police officers rely on this database every day to find missing people and catch criminals, so a hack could put public safety and private information at risk.

A cyberattack is an attack on computers or computer systems by hackers.
